text:
maya (People Ops): Hi all — launching a 4-month pilot for Compassionate Care Leave + Emergency Travel Assistance, effective 2026-06-01. Quick summary: up to 5 paid Compassionate Care days (separate from PTO) per rolling 12 months for major family emergencies, plus a one-time Emergency Travel Reimbursement (up to $750) per qualifying event. Details below and link to policy. :heart:

elena (People Ops): Who qualifies? Is this global?

maya (People Ops): Available to all regular employees (FT & part-time 20+ hrs/wk) and apprentices. Contractors excluded. Applies worldwide but reimbursement processing varies by region — see the doc for country-specific notes.

tom (Finance): Heads up: reimbursements >$600 will be reported per US tax rules; Finance will handle forms. We'll try to minimize tax impact but teams should expect standard reporting where required.

raj (Legal): Documentation needed: brief attestation of the emergency (employee-submitted) and receipts for travel. We won't require medical records in most cases to respect privacy. Legal review OK with this approach.

devon (Manager): Can compassionate days be taken intermittently (e.g., 2 days now, 3 later)?

elena (People Ops): Yes — flexible use within the 12-month window, but managers should coordinate coverage. Managers approve within 48 hours; escalate if urgent.

maya (People Ops): Reimbursement rules: up to $750 for travel/urgent lodging/caregiver transport. Use Expensify with tag "Compassionate-Travel". If receipts cannot be provided in extreme circumstances, managers can request an advance via the People Ops portal and attach an explanation.

ops-bot: Policy doc published: https://docs.redwood.company/people-ops/compassionate-care-travel-pilot — v1.0 (2026-06-01).

tom (Finance): Note to managers: international payroll advances may take 5-7 business days in some countries; use the advance option for time-sensitive cases.

raj (Legal): Also flag for visa holders — any paid leave must comply with local immigration rules. People Ops will coordinate with Employment Counsel on a case-by-case basis.

devon (Manager): Thanks — will share with my team. Is there a central tracker for usage?

elena (People Ops): Yes, we'll track number of events, average reimbursement, and manager feedback. Review planned for 2026-10-01 to decide permanent policy.

maya (People Ops): Please DM with edge cases (cross-border guardianship, long-term care) or post in #help-people-ops. We'll also add an FAQ to onboarding and update the People Ops handbook.

devon (Manager): Appreciate it. One ask: can we get a sample manager response/approval wording to use in threads?
\melena (People Ops): Typo — elena (People Ops): Yep, sample responses are in the doc under "Manager Guidance" (copyable snippets).

maya (People Ops): Thank you all. We're aiming for compassionate, low-friction support. Reach out with questions. :pray:
